findings.text: non-blocking: _runs_on at this line looks up run_rows on the (slug, section) pair and a plan-level ref uses section "" which no dispatch pointer carries, so why(alpha) silently answers runs: [] while alpha#s3 is held; an empty list reads as "nobody is working on it".

non-blocking: the view vocabulary and its size contract are forked into WHY_VIEW and WHY_VIEW_BUDGET, while reckon/mcp_views.py:52 VIEW_NAMES and reckon/mcp_budget.py:22 VIEW_BUDGETS carry no "why" row, so the per-view fit test never enumerates it and the plan's "within its row of the §2 table" has no row; the worker records this under outside_scope and it needs a node.

non-blocking: the waits are read from the raw section_depends_on map rather than the roadmap's _section_scoped_edges (reckon/roadmap.py:1446), so the kinds the module docstring claims -- gate, decision, run-blocked -- are never emitted and the why answer can disagree with a roadmap row about whether a section is held.

non-blocking: the size assertion compares the answer to WHY_VIEW_BUDGET, the constant _fit_why trims to, so a regression raising that constant keeps the test green; line 256 has the same shape against MAX_EVENTS and the goal's five, so neither declared figure is guarded from an independent source.

non-blocking: the constant's comment reads "the goal fixes this at five", citing the dispatch goal a future reader has no access to, where the mechanism (at most five events per answer) is the fact worth stating.
